outcome: gut microbiota composition (intestinal dysbiosis, abundance of specific bacteria like Lactobacillus, Bifidobacterium, Enterococcus, Klebsiella species, Escherichia coli)
cohort: The study included 134 infants, with 82 diagnosed with functional gastrointestinal disorders (FGIDs) and 52 without FGIDs.
finding: Infants with functional gastrointestinal disorders exhibited an imbalance of intestinal microflora, characterized by decreased acidifying bacteria (Lactobacillus, Bifidobacterium, Enterococcus) and increased proteolytic microorganisms (Klebsiella species, Escherichia coli).
mod_finding: Infants born by cesarean section showed a significantly higher incidence of functional gastrointestinal disorders and intestinal dysbiosis.
